subject: maths
title: Decimal problems with money and measurement

scenes.heading: Decimal problems: money and measurement
scenes.sub: Is the bigger bottle really better value?
scenes.say: Is the big bottle of juice really better value? Real problems never come as neat sums. Today you will plan multi-step money and measurement problems, and get every decimal right.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: A recipe: ingredients, steps in order, then taste-test
scenes.science: A problem: numbers with units, plan the steps, check the answer
scenes.breaks: A recipe tells you the steps. In a problem you choose the steps yourself, and sometimes run them backwards.
scenes.say: A good recipe lists the ingredients, then the steps in order, and you taste-test at the end. Solve problems the same way: list the numbers with their units, plan the steps, then check the answer makes sense. The analogy breaks down because a recipe gives you the steps, but in a problem you have to choose them yourself.

scenes.heading: Unit price
scenes.say: To compare value, find the unit price: the price divided by the amount. Use the same unit for both, like dollars per litre. The lower unit price is the best buy, even if that pack costs more in total.

scenes.heading: Best buy
scenes.question: Juice: 1.5 L for $3.45 or 2 L for $4.40. Which is better value?
lines: The 2 L bottle is the best buy
scenes.say: One and a half litres for three dollars forty-five is two dollars thirty per litre. Two litres for four dollars forty is two dollars twenty per litre. Two twenty is lower, so the two litre bottle is the best buy.
scenes.caption: 1.5 L for $3.45 is $2.30 per litre. 2 L for $4.40 is $2.20 per litre. $2.20 is lower, so the 2 L bottle is the best buy.

scenes.heading: Cash rounding to 5 cents
points: Ends in 1 or 2: round down to 0
Ends in 3 or 4: round up to 5
Ends in 6 or 7: round down to 5
Ends in 8 or 9: round up to 0
scenes.say: Australia has no one or two cent coins, so cash totals round to the nearest five cents. Twenty-seven eighty-three becomes twenty-seven eighty-five. Card payments are not rounded. And only round once, at the very end.
scenes.caption: Australia has no 1c or 2c coins, so cash totals round to the nearest 5 cents. $27.83 becomes $27.85. Card payments are not rounded. And only round once, at the very end.

scenes.heading: Working backwards
scenes.question: Leo buys 3 snacks at $4.65 each and has $6.25 left. How much did he start with?
scenes.say: Leo spent three times four dollars sixty-five, which is thirteen ninety-five. To undo spending, add it back: six twenty-five plus thirteen ninety-five is twenty dollars twenty.
scenes.caption: Leo spent 3 × $4.65 = $13.95. To undo spending, add it back: $6.25 + $13.95 = $20.20.

points: Round money once, at the end
scenes.say: Quick recap. List every number with its unit and plan before you calculate. Compare value with unit prices. Convert units before adding or comparing. Round money once, at the end. And work backwards with opposite operations. Now try the practice questions!
